record.paper_title: Report from the Open Problems Session at OPSFA13
record.original_question: Let δ > 0, λ > 0, n ∈ N_0, and for 0 < t < π define F_n^{λ,δ}(t) = ∫_0^t (t-θ)^δ C_n^λ(cos θ) (sin θ)^{2λ} dθ, where C_n^λ is the Gegenbauer polynomial. Is it true that F_n^{λ,δ}(t) > 0 for all t in (0, π] if and only if δ ≥ λ + 1?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.1. Let δ > 0, λ > 0 and n ∈ N0. For every 0 < t < π, deﬁne F λ,δ n (t) = ∫ t 0 (t−θ)δ C λ n (cos θ)(sin θ)2λ dθ. Then F λ,δ n (t) > 0 for all t in (0, π] if and only if δ ≥ λ + 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For real parameters $\delta>0$ and $\lambda>0$, and a nonnegative integer $n$, let $C_n^{\lambda}$ denote the Gegenbauer (ultraspherical) polynomial of degree $n$ and index $\lambda$, defined by the generating function
$$(1-2xr+r^2)^{-\lambda}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} C_n^{\lambda}(x)\,r^n,\qquad |r|<1,\ x\in[-1,1].$$
For $0<t\le\pi$ define
$$F_n^{\lambda,\delta}(t)=\int_0^t (t-\theta)^{\delta}\, C_n^{\lambda}(\cos\theta)\,(\sin\theta)^{2\lambda}\, d\theta.$$
Determine whether the following equivalence holds: for every $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$ and every $t\in(0,\pi]$,
$$F_n^{\lambda,\delta}(t)>0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \delta\ge \lambda+1.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The sufficiency direction (positivity of the integral when δ ≥ λ+1) was established by Buhmann, Cardington, and Filbir (arXiv:1701.00787), in the more general Jacobi setting, thereby proving one direction of the conjecture. The necessity direction (that δ ≥ λ+1 is required for positivity for all n and all t ∈ (0,π]) does not appear to be settled by that work, so the full equivalence remains only partially verified.

status_evidence.title: Positive definite functions on the unit sphere and integrals of Jacobi polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Proves that integrals of Jacobi polynomials of the form ∫_0^t (t-θ)^δ P_n^{(α-1/2,β-1/2)}(cos θ)(sin(θ/2))^{2α}(cos(θ/2))^{2β} dθ are positive for δ ≥ α+1, confirming the Gegenbauer-integral conjecture in the sufficiency direction.
status_evidence.claim: The sufficient condition δ ≥ λ+1 for positivity of F_n^{λ,δ}(t) on (0,π] has been proved.
